drills.tip: English SVO becomes Korean SOV. The verb goes at the end.
Subject marker 이 after a consonant-final noun.
Object marker 를 after a vowel-final noun.
Even with no object, the verb still comes last.

drills.en: As for me, I am a student.
drills.tip: 는 marks the topic. Copula 이에요 after a consonant.

drills.en: As for Korean, it is fun.
drills.tip: Topic 는 frames; no separate subject needed.
오늘 is topic; 날씨 is the grammatical subject.
저는 frames the liker; 커피를 is the object.
에 marks destination. Particles follow the noun.
에서 marks where an action happens.
에서 also means from with motion verbs.

drills.en: I go to Jeju by plane.
drills.tip: 로 marks means. After a vowel, use 로.
하고 means with or and, after the noun.
도 also replaces 은/는 or 이/가.
Typical order: topic, time, place, object, verb.
Subject can drop. Verb stays last.
Past polite still sits at the end.
Time adverb before object and verb.

drills.en: In the morning I drink coffee.
drills.tip: 에 marks parts of the day.

drills.en: Because it rains, I take a taxi.
drills.tip: Reason clause -아서/어서 before the main verb.
친절하다 becomes 친절한 before the noun.

drills.en: I go to a big school.
drills.tip: 크다 becomes 큰 before the noun.

drills.en: I do not eat spicy food.
drills.tip: 맵다 becomes 매운. 안 before the verb.
Korean often drops the subject when it is obvious.
Object stays marked; subject can vanish.
부터 and 까지 come AFTER the noun.
Location nouns follow the reference noun, then take 에.
English next to X becomes X 옆에.
안 inside is a postposition-like noun.
위 above/on comes after the noun.

drills.en: I study from morning until night.
The book is on the desk.
There is a store near the school.
Before lunch I wash my hands.

drills.tip: Shopping staple. 예요 after a vowel.
이해가 안 돼요 is the natural phrasing.
살다 is ㄹ-irregular. 에 for residence.

drills.en: I go to school by bus.
How do I get to the airport?
drills.tip: 어떻게 before the verb of motion.

drills.en: I can speak a little Korean.
I will teach English in Jeju.
drills.tip: Future with place 에서 and object 를.

drills.en: I need to find a used car.
I buy tangerines at the market.
The wifi password is on the wall.
I drink coffee at a cafe.
Do you have this in a bigger size?
I get off at City Hall.
Please write it on the board.
